reasoning: Recent high-quality polling of Maine’s 2026 U.S. Senate race consistently shows Democrat Troy Jackson holding a very small edge over Republican Sen. Susan Collins, typically in the low single digits and within the margin of error, so the race is effectively a toss-up but currently leans narrowly D in polling terms. There is no fresh, state-specific presidential general-election polling in the last 45 days in the results provided, so the best structural guide for that is Maine’s D+3 Cook PVI, indicating a slight underlying Democratic advantage statewide. Synthesizing these sources, the current measurable margin is a roughly D+2 to D+3 environment for the Maine Senate race, with no separate, recent quantified presidential margin available for just this state.

sources.name: Fox News
sources.details: Fox News poll of Maine’s 2026 Senate race finds Troy Jackson at 48% and Susan Collins at 46%, a D+2 edge well within the survey’s ±3% margin of error.

sources.name: Hart Research Associates / Senate Majority PAC (reported by Newsweek)
sources.details: Hart Research Associates poll for Senate Majority PAC shows Jackson leading Collins 49% to 45%, a D+4 margin among 802 likely Maine voters.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center (reported by Portland Press Herald)
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Pine Tree State Poll finds Jackson at 49% and Collins at 46% among likely general-election voters, a D+3 Senate margin in Maine.

sources.name: Spectrum Local News / UNH Pine Tree State Poll
sources.details: Spectrum Local News summary of the UNH Pine Tree State Poll reports Jackson leading Collins 49% to 46%, describing the Maine Senate race as a statistical tie.

sources.name: Bangor Daily News / UNH Survey Center
sources.details: Bangor Daily News coverage notes the UNH poll shows Jackson at 49% and Collins at 46% in a close Maine Senate contest.

sources.details: The Hill reports on the UNH survey finding Jackson leading Collins 49% to 46% among likely Maine general-election voters in the 2026 Senate race.

sources.details: UNH Survey Center release indicates Jackson and Collins are statistically tied in a November Senate matchup while Jackson is preferred by most Democratic primary voters as the nominee.

sources.name: Newsweek (summarizing Fox News and Hart Research polling)
sources.details: Newsweek piece on new Maine Senate polling reports a Fox News survey with Jackson 48% and Collins 46% (D+2) and reiterates the Hart Research poll showing Jackson 49% to Collins 45% (D+4), highlighting Collins’s slipping position.

sources.name: Public Policy Polling (reported by Newsweek)
sources.details: Public Policy Polling survey, as summarized by Newsweek, finds Jackson leading Collins 49% to 44% in Maine’s Senate race, a D+5 margin among 785 registered voters shortly after the Platner scandals.

sources.details: Newsweek’s discussion of the Hart Research poll reiterates Jackson’s 49% to 45% lead over Collins and notes 6% of Maine likely voters undecided, underscoring a competitive but D-tilting Senate race.

sources.details: BizPac Review coverage of the UNH ‘Pine Tree State Poll’ reports Jackson at 49% and Collins at 46% (D+3) and notes Collins’s net-negative favorability in Maine.

sources.details: USA Today article on younger voters in Maine’s Senate race cites the UNH poll showing Jackson in a statistical dead heat with Collins and strong support among voters ages 18-34.
